1.title: How Does a Computer *Know It's Correct?*

stages.line: A student scored 85. The pass mark is 40. Is 85 alone enough to tell?
stages.right: No. Knowing the marks alone is not enough.
stages.wrong: Does 85 say anything about the pass mark?

stages.line: What else do we need to know?
stages.right: The passing requirement: 40 marks.
stages.wrong: What do we compare the marks with?

stages.line: Now what should the computer check?

options.text: Whether the marks are at least 40.

stages.right: It checks the marks against the requirement.
stages.wrong: The requirement is the passing mark.

stages.line: Change the marks. Is the passing requirement satisfied?

props.hint: Is the marks at least 40?

finishPanel.title: Checked!
finishPanel.text: A program often checks information against a requirement to see if it is satisfied.

stages.line: Each question asks us to check something. Tap each one.

scenes.label: Is the number positive?
scenes.caption: Whether the number is greater than zero.

scenes.label: Is the number even?
scenes.caption: Whether the remainder after dividing by 2 is zero.

scenes.label: Is the account verified?
scenes.caption: Whether the verification status is True.

finishPanel.title: Things we can check!
finishPanel.text: Each question can be answered as correct or incorrect.

stages.line: In programming, what is a condition?

options.text: An expression that is True or False.
A number stored in a program.

stages.right: A condition checks whether a statement or requirement is True or False.
stages.wrong: A condition is something we can check, and the check gives an answer.

3.title: Can a Statement Be *True and False?*

stages.line: Evaluate each question. Tap a row.

finishPanel.title: One result!
finishPanel.text: A condition gives one Boolean result. It can't be True and False at once.

stages.line: Three new questions. Predict each result.

props.hint: Is the statement correct?

finishPanel.title: True or False!
finishPanel.text: Conditions are evaluated as Boolean results: True or False.

stages.line: Information tells us what we have. Tap each to see a check we could ask.
Does age = 17 check a requirement?
stages.right: No. It only tells us what we have. age >= 18 would check a requirement.
stages.wrong: Does it ask a question, or just state a value?

stages.line: What is the difference between information and a condition?

options.text: Information tells what we have; a condition checks a requirement.

stages.right: A condition checks whether information satisfies a requirement.
stages.wrong: One of them stores a value, and the other asks a question about it.

stages.line: A condition is built step by step, not memorised. Follow the path.

steps.title: Find the relationship
steps.text: A positive number is greater than zero.

steps.title: Say it in words
steps.text: The number must be greater than zero.

stages.line: Check whether a number is greater than 5. Put the steps in order.

props.hint: Understand the requirement first. The Python comes near the end.

finishPanel.title: Understand first!
finishPanel.text: We understand the requirement, then build its Python.

stages.line: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 are positive numbers. Where are they compared with zero?
stages.right: All positive numbers appear after zero on the number line.
stages.wrong: Look at the number line. Which side of zero are they on?

stages.line: Numbers to the right of zero are greater than zero. So a positive number must be…
stages.right: A positive number is greater than zero.
stages.wrong: Positive numbers come after zero.

stages.line: The number must be greater than zero. Build it in Python.

props.hint: Greater than zero: which symbol?

finishPanel.title: number > 0
finishPanel.text: > means greater than, because the number must be greater than zero.

stages.line: Test it. Is number > 0 True?

props.hint: Is the number greater than zero?

finishPanel.title: Zero is neither!
finishPanel.text: Zero is neither positive nor negative.

stages.line: -1, -2, -3… are on the left of zero. How do they compare with zero?
stages.right: Negative numbers are smaller than zero.
stages.wrong: They come before zero on the number line.

stages.line: The number must be less than zero. Build it in Python.

props.hint: Smaller than zero: which symbol?

finishPanel.title: number < 0
finishPanel.text: < means less than, because the number must be smaller than zero.

stages.line: Test it. Is number < 0 True?

props.hint: Is the number smaller than zero?

stages.line: We want exactly 7. Is 8 acceptable?
stages.right: Only 7 is exactly equal to 7.
stages.wrong: We don't want a number greater or smaller than 7.

stages.line: The number must be equal to 7. Build it in Python.

props.hint: Exactly equal: use ==, not a single =.

finishPanel.title: number == 7
finishPanel.text: == checks equality. A single = is for assignment, not for comparing.

stages.line: Test it. Is number == 7 True?

props.hint: Is the number exactly 7?

finishPanel.title: Only 7!
finishPanel.text: The condition is True only when the number is exactly 7.

stages.line: A game accepts every number except 7. Is 7 acceptable?
stages.right: Every number except 7 is fine. 7 is rejected.
stages.wrong: The game accepts every number except 7.

stages.line: The number must be different from 7. Build it in Python.

props.hint: Different from 7: which symbol?

finishPanel.title: number != 7
finishPanel.text: != means not equal to. It checks that two values are different.

stages.line: Test it. Is number != 7 True?

props.hint: Is the number different from 7?

finishPanel.title: Not 7!
finishPanel.text: The condition is True whenever the number is different from 7.

stages.line: A competition needs a score of at least 10. Who can qualify?

props.hint: At least 10 means 10 or more.

stages.line: The score must be greater than or equal to 10. Build it.

props.hint: At least includes 10: which symbol?

finishPanel.title: number >= 10
finishPanel.text: >= combines greater than and equal to.

stages.line: Boundary test. Is number >= 10 True?

props.hint: Is the number 10 or more?

finishPanel.title: Boundary included!
finishPanel.text: At least means the minimum boundary is included.

stages.line: A bag holds at most 10 chocolates. Which amounts fit?

props.hint: At most 10 means 10 or fewer.

stages.line: The number must be less than or equal to 10. Build it.

props.hint: At most includes 10: which symbol?

finishPanel.title: number <= 10
finishPanel.text: <= means less than or equal to.

stages.line: Boundary test. Is number <= 10 True?

props.hint: Is the number 10 or fewer?

finishPanel.title: Boundary included!
finishPanel.text: At most means the maximum boundary is included.

13.title: How Can We Spot an *Even Number?*

stages.line: Share each number of objects into two equal groups. Tap a number.
What is common among even numbers like 6, 8 and 10?

options.text: They share into two equal groups with nothing left.

stages.right: Even numbers are completely divisible by 2. There is no remainder.
stages.wrong: Look at what happened to 6, 8 and 10, and then to 7.

stages.line: % gives the remainder. Predict each remainder.

props.hint: Share into groups of 2. What is left?

finishPanel.title: Remainders!
finishPanel.text: Even numbers leave a remainder of 0 when divided by 2.

stages.line: The remainder must be zero. First find it, then check it.

props.hint: First number % 2, then == 0.

finishPanel.title: number % 2 == 0
finishPanel.text: % 2 finds the remainder. == 0 checks that nothing remains.

stages.line: Test it. Is number % 2 == 0 True?

props.hint: What remains when you divide by 2?

finishPanel.title: Even!
finishPanel.text: A number is even when its remainder after division by 2 is zero.

15.title: What Happens When a Number Is *Odd?*

stages.line: Share 7, then 9 objects into two groups. Predict each remainder.

props.hint: Share into two groups. What is left?

stages.line: An odd number leaves a remainder that is not zero. Build it.

props.hint: The remainder must not be zero: use !=.

finishPanel.title: number % 2 != 0
finishPanel.text: % 2 finds the remainder. != 0 checks that it is not zero.

stages.line: Test it. Is number % 2 != 0 True?

props.hint: Does it leave a remainder when divided by 2?

finishPanel.title: Odd!
finishPanel.text: An odd integer has a nonzero remainder when divided by 2.

stages.line: Check whether a number is divisible by 5.

props.hint: Divisible means no remainder: % first, then == 0.
props.prompt: Hint: % finds the remainder, == checks equality.

finishPanel.title: number % 5 == 0
finishPanel.text: % 5 finds the remainder, and == 0 says nothing is left. So 5 divides the number.

stages.line: Check whether a number is not divisible by 3.

props.hint: Not divisible means something is left: % first, then != 0.
props.prompt: Hint: % finds the remainder, != checks it is not zero.

finishPanel.title: number % 3 != 0
finishPanel.text: % 3 finds the remainder, and != 0 says something is left. So 3 doesn't divide it.

stages.line: Check whether a number is greater than 100.

props.hint: Greater than means more than, and 100 itself is not included.

finishPanel.title: number > 100
finishPanel.text: > is used because the number must be bigger than 100. >= would let 100 in.

stages.line: Check whether a number is equal to 50.

props.hint: Equal to compares two values: which symbol?

finishPanel.title: number == 50
finishPanel.text: == compares the number with 50. A single = would give a value a name instead.

17.title: What If One Requirement *Is Not Enough?*

stages.line: “I need ice cream AND pastry. Both.” Try each case.

props.ask: Is my complete dessert order satisfied?
props.hint: I asked for both. Do I have both?

finishPanel.title: Both needed!
finishPanel.text: Both requirements must be satisfied.

stages.line: All four possibilities. Tap each row to see the order.

finishPanel.title: AND!
finishPanel.text: AND gives True only when both conditions are True.

stages.line: Python's word for “both” is and. Build the condition.

props.hint: Both must be True: connect them with and.

finishPanel.title: ice_cream and pastry
finishPanel.text: and connects two conditions when both requirements must be satisfied.

stages.line: “Extra class on Sunday if Anjali OR Ravi comes.” Try each case.

props.hint: The class needs just one of them. Is anyone coming?

cases.true: At least one comes: the class happens.

finishPanel.title: Only one needed!
finishPanel.text: Only one of the two needs to come for the requirement to be True.

stages.line: All four possibilities. Tap each row.

finishPanel.title: OR!
finishPanel.text: OR gives True when at least one condition is True.

stages.line: Python's word for “at least one” is or. Build the condition.

props.hint: One is enough: connect them with or.

finishPanel.title: anjali_comes or ravi_comes
finishPanel.text: or connects conditions when at least one requirement must be satisfied.

stages.line: Same two conditions, two words. Tap each row.

finishPanel.title: AND vs OR
finishPanel.text: AND needs both True. OR needs at least one True.

stages.line: “Both items are required.” Which operator fits?
stages.right: and: both conditions must be True.
stages.wrong: Both must be satisfied, not just one.

stages.line: “Either one is enough.” Which operator fits?
stages.right: or: at least one condition must be True.
stages.wrong: Only one needs to be satisfied.

stages.line: Ice cream: True. Pastry: False. The order still counts. Which operator?
stages.right: or: one True condition is enough.
stages.wrong: With and, one False would break the order.

stages.line: A score must be between 10 and 20, both included. Who qualifies?

props.hint: Is it inside the highlighted range, ends included?

stages.line: What two requirements must a valid score meet?
stages.right: A range needs two comparisons: at least 10, and at most 20.
stages.wrong: A valid score is not below 10 and not above 20.

stages.line: Step 1: the lower boundary. The number must be at least 10.

props.hint: At least 10 includes 10: which symbol?

finishPanel.title: number >= 10
finishPanel.text: >= includes the lower boundary.

stages.line: Step 2: the upper boundary. The number must be at most 20.

props.hint: At most 20 includes 20: which symbol?

finishPanel.title: number <= 20
finishPanel.text: <= includes the upper boundary.

stages.line: Step 3: must both be True? Yes. Combine them.

props.hint: Both must be True: connect them with and.

finishPanel.title: Both must be True
finishPanel.text: and requires both comparisons to be True.

stages.line: Test it. Is the condition True?

props.hint: Is it at least 10, and at most 20?

finishPanel.title: Both included!
finishPanel.text: Both 10 and 20 are included.

stages.line: At least 10 but less than 20. Which are acceptable?

props.hint: At least 10 allows 10. Less than 20 does not allow 20.

stages.line: Build it: at least 10, and less than 20.

props.hint: Use >= for the first boundary and < for the second.

finishPanel.title: number >= 10 and number < 20
finishPanel.text: The exact words decide whether a boundary is included or excluded.

stages.line: Greater than 10 and smaller than 20. Which are allowed?

props.hint: Greater than 10 leaves out 10. Smaller than 20 leaves out 20.

stages.line: Build it: greater than 10, and smaller than 20.

props.hint: Use > and < so both boundaries stay out.

finishPanel.title: number > 10 and number < 20
finishPanel.text: > and < leave both boundaries out.

stages.line: “At least 10 and at most 20.” Which condition?
stages.right: >= and <= include both boundaries.
stages.wrong: At least and at most both include their number.

stages.line: “At least 10 but less than 20.” Which condition?
stages.right: The comparison symbols control whether the boundary values are included.
stages.wrong: 10 is allowed, 20 is not.

26.title: What If a Number Is *Outside 10 to 20?*

stages.line: Accepted only if smaller than 10 OR greater than 20. Which are accepted?

props.hint: Is it smaller than 10, or greater than 20?

stages.line: Build it: smaller than 10, or greater than 20.

props.hint: A number can be outside on either side: use or.

finishPanel.title: number < 10 or number > 20
finishPanel.text: Each side is one comparison, joined by or.

stages.line: Why is OR the right word here?

options.text: A number can be outside on either side.

stages.right: Outside the range means being on the left or on the right.
stages.wrong: Can a number be smaller than 10 and greater than 20 at once?

27.title: What Happens When We *Reverse a Statement?*

stages.line: Switch the statement between True and False. What does the reversed one become?

props.ask: “Ravi will NOT come to class.” Is this True?
props.hint: Flip it: if the first statement is True, the reversed one is…?

finishPanel.title: NOT reverses!
finishPanel.text: NOT reverses a Boolean result.

stages.line: Python reverses with the word not. Build: not ravi_comes.

props.hint: Put not before the condition it reverses.

finishPanel.title: not ravi_comes
finishPanel.text: If ravi_comes is True, the whole expression is False. If it is False, the expression is True.

stages.line: The truth table for not. Tap each row.

finishPanel.title: NOT!
finishPanel.text: The not operator reverses the Boolean result of the expression after it.

29.title: What If a Number Is *NOT Greater Than 10?*

stages.line: 15 > 10 is True. What does not (15 > 10) give?
stages.right: False. not reverses the result of 15 > 10.
stages.wrong: First find 15 > 10, then reverse it.

stages.line: Test it. Is not (number > 10) True?

props.hint: First find number > 10, then reverse the result.

stages.line: Build it: not, then the comparison in parentheses.

props.hint: Put the comparison in parentheses, with not in front.

finishPanel.title: not (number > 10)
finishPanel.text: The parentheses group the comparison so not applies to all of it. != checks inequality directly; not reverses another condition.

stages.line: Marks at least 40 AND attendance at least 75. Must both be met?
stages.right: Yes. There are two requirements, and both are needed.
stages.wrong: It says AND. Does one requirement alone do?

stages.line: Build each requirement, then connect them.

props.hint: Both must be True: connect them with and.

finishPanel.title: Smaller parts!
finishPanel.text: marks >= 40 and attendance >= 75. A complex condition connects smaller conditions.

stages.line: Does each student qualify?

props.hint: Both requirements must be met.

stages.line: Reward if the score is exactly 100 OR all bonus tasks are done. Must both happen?
stages.right: No. Either one is enough.
stages.wrong: It says OR. Is one enough?

stages.line: Build it: score exactly 100, or the bonus tasks done.

props.hint: Either is enough: connect them with or.

finishPanel.title: Alternatives!
finishPanel.text: score == 100 or bonus_tasks_completed. or can join different kinds of conditions, not just comparisons.

stages.line: Does the student get the reward?

props.hint: One True requirement is enough.

stages.line: Age 10 to 20, inclusive, OR special permission. Group the age part.

props.hint: The age range goes in parentheses, then or special_permission.

finishPanel.title: Groups!
finishPanel.text: The parentheses group the two age requirements. That group is then joined to special_permission with or.

stages.line: Test different combinations. Does the student qualify?

props.hint: Is the age in range, or is there permission?

finishPanel.title: Organised!
finishPanel.text: Parentheses help organise complex conditions into meaningful groups.

stages.line: Age 15 to 20 AND registered, OR special permission. Which go together?
stages.right: Age and registration must be met together. Special permission is a separate alternative.
stages.wrong: Which two parts are joined by AND?

stages.line: Build the whole condition. Group what must be True together.

props.hint: Age and registered go in the parentheses. Then or special_permission.

finishPanel.title: One condition!
finishPanel.text: A long requirement splits into smaller logical parts that combine into one condition.

stages.line: A student has special permission but is outside the age range. Can they join?
stages.right: Yes. Special permission can satisfy the condition on its own.
stages.wrong: Which part of the condition does special permission satisfy?

stages.line: At least 10 and at most 20. A learner wrote this. Is it True?

props.hint: Check both comparisons for that number.

stages.line: What is wrong with this condition?

options.text: It uses or instead of and.

stages.right: The requirement includes both boundaries, but this condition leaves them out.
stages.wrong: Look at what happened to 10 and 20.

stages.line: Fix it: at least 10 and at most 20.

props.hint: Both boundaries must be included: use >= and <=.

finishPanel.title: Fixed!
finishPanel.text: A condition can look almost correct but still fail at the boundary values.

stages.line: Between 10 and 20, both included. A learner wrote this. Is it True?

props.hint: With or, one True comparison is enough.

stages.line: 5 and 25 are outside the range, yet get True. Why?

options.text: With or, one True comparison is enough.

stages.right: One comparison can be True even when the number is outside the required range.
stages.wrong: Check each comparison for 5 and for 25.

stages.line: Fix it: both range requirements must be True together.

props.hint: Both must be True at the same time: use and.

finishPanel.title: Both together!
finishPanel.text: Both range requirements must be satisfied at the same time.

stages.line: Check whether a person is at least 18 years old.

props.hint: At least 18 includes 18: which symbol?

finishPanel.title: age >= 18
finishPanel.text: >= is used because 18 itself is old enough: at least 18.

stages.line: Check whether a number is negative.

props.hint: Negative means smaller than zero.

finishPanel.title: number < 0
finishPanel.text: < is used because negative numbers are smaller than zero.

stages.line: Check whether a number is even.

props.hint: Even means nothing remains when dividing by 2.

finishPanel.title: number % 2 == 0
finishPanel.text: % 2 finds the remainder, and == 0 says nothing is left.

stages.line: Check whether a number is greater than 50 but at most 100.

props.hint: Two parts, both True: greater than 50, and at most 100.

finishPanel.title: A range!
finishPanel.text: number > 50 and number <= 100. > leaves 50 out, <= keeps 100 in, and and needs both.

stages.line: A student can take part if they completed the project OR scored at least 80.

props.hint: Either one is enough: connect them with or.

finishPanel.title: Alternatives!
finishPanel.text: project_completed or score >= 80. or: either is enough; >= because at least 80 includes 80.

stages.line: Eligible if age is 18 to 30, inclusive, AND the account is verified.

props.hint: All three parts must be True: use and between them.

finishPanel.title: Three parts!
finishPanel.text: age >= 18 and age <= 30 and account_verified. and needs all three to be True.

stages.line: Check whether a number is NOT between 10 and 20, including both.

props.hint: Build the range inside parentheses, then put not in front.

finishPanel.title: Reversed range!
finishPanel.text: not (number >= 10 and number <= 20). not reverses the whole range check; the parentheses group it.

stages.line: Score at least 80 AND project done, OR special permission.

props.hint: The AND part goes in parentheses, then or special_permission.

finishPanel.title: Well designed!
finishPanel.text: (score >= 80 and project_completed) or special_permission. The group needs both; permission is an alternative.

stages.line: Your toolkit. Tap an operator to see what it does.

items.title: At least one must be True

stages.line: Three kinds of condition you can build. Tap each.

finishPanel.title: You can build conditions!
finishPanel.text: A good programmer understands the requirement, splits it into parts, picks the operators and builds the condition.
